_comment: One definition of 'an actual is never written on or across a band', held by neither language: Digits.beside (Java: the CI/CD JSON - a client actual at two decimals, a server actual at four - JUnit, the LOAD_NOT_ACHIEVED sentence) and WIR.digits.beside (report.js: both tabs). beside(value, decimals, bands): value rounded to `decimals` as Math.round rounds, an exact tie upward (written as it is once value*10^decimals passes 2^53), unless that number is on a band the value is not on, or across one; then the fewest significant digits, from the rounded number's own count up to max(12, a third decimal) and never past 17, that keep it on its side of every band, each the double's exact value rounded half away from zero. A band of 0 is never-zero.

_bandWriteComment: L12: how a band's own constant is WRITTEN in every sentence that quotes it (not to be confused with assert-parity-vectors.json's bandTextCases, a band READ from text) - Predicate.describe's Predicate.trim (Java: Usability's and KpiUsability's sentences, the LOAD_NOT_ACHIEVED sentence and JUnit, and so the CI/CD JSON's reasons and findings) and WIR.javaText.trim (report.js: both tabs). In plain digits: an integral band below 2^63 in magnitude is every digit of its exact value (2^62 is 4611686018427387904, not the shortest digits padded with zeros), and any other band - every non-integral one, and an integral one at or past 2^63, which the long cast used to saturate (1e19 read 9223372036854775807) - is Double.toString's shortest digits without the E notation it uses below 1e-3 and from 1e7 (1e23 is 100000000000000000000000, as the tables' formatBand writes it, not the nearest double's exact 99999999999999991611392). Compared as text. DigitsTest and digits.test.js run these; the parity vectors' detail and warnings sentences hold the same spelling inside a sentence.

bandWriteCases.name: an integral band has no .0
negative zero is 0
a decimal band in Double.toString's plain range is that text
a negative decimal band keeps every digit, ungrouped
1e-3 is the edge Double.toString writes plain

two significant digits far below 1e-3
a decimal band just under 1e7 was plain already
a decimal band far past 1e7
an integral band from 1e7 was a long's digits already
2^62 keeps every digit, not the shortest padded with zeros (4611686018427388000)
the last double below 2^63 keeps every digit, not the shortest padded with zeros (9223372036854775000)
2^63 is where the shortest digits take over: 9.223372036854776E18 written out, neither its exact 9223372036854775808 nor the 9223372036854775807 the long cast saturated to
-2^63 is 2^63 by magnitude: the shortest digits, not the long's minimum -9223372036854775808
1e19 is 1.0E19 written out, not saturated
-1e19 is -1.0E19 written out, not saturated at the long's minimum
1e22 is 1.0E22 written out
1e23 is not a double: the band is the double nearest it, written as Double.toString's 1.0E23 - not that double's exact 99999999999999991611392
past 2^63 a band with more digits than a double holds is its shortest digits padded with zeros, not its exact 12345678901234567741440
